_provenance.purpose: Cross-language Avro wire-compatibility fixture for conduit.schema.AvroSchema (WS2). A Python-only round-trip is not evidence of Go interop, so these bytes were produced by an actual Go program using github.com/hamba/avro/v2 -- the exact library conduit-commons' schema/avro package wraps (schema/avro/serde.go: avro.ParseBytes + avro.Marshal/avro.Unmarshal) -- not reimplemented or guessed at from the Avro spec.
_provenance.generator_note: The Go generator program (not checked into this repo) parsed `schema_json` below with avro.ParseBytes, then called avro.Marshal(schema, v) on each case's Go struct value, round-tripping through avro.Unmarshal as a sanity gate before recording the hex output. See tests/test_schema_avro.py for how these bytes are consumed and what each assertion proves.
_provenance.array_framing_note: hamba/avro encodes the non-empty `tags` array (case with_note) using Avro's negative-block-count + explicit-byte-size framing (spec-legal, used for reader skip-ahead); fastavro's schemaless_writer instead uses the plain positive-count framing (also spec-legal). Both were verified bidirectionally decodable during golden generation (fastavro decoded the Go bytes; a companion Go decoder program decoded fastavro's own encoding of the same value) even though the two encoders' output isn't byte-identical for that one field. The `null_note` case has an empty array (`tags: []`), where this ambiguity doesn't arise (block count 0 either way), and is fully byte-exact in both directions -- see test_schema_avro.py's assertions.
